newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Techs eye topping formation in dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Techs eye topping formation in dlr/mark.

text.p: Technicians expect the dollar to get a modest bid if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates on Tuesday, but are eyeing a head-and-shoulders topping pattern in dollar/mark which could keep gains limited.
Initial resistance lurks near 1.6930 marks, but chartists said the dollar should encounter stronger resistance if it moves above 1.70 marks.
"It looks like a clear head-and-shoulders top could form," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America, predicting resistance between the 1.7030 and 1.7050 area.
Johnson said a move above this threshold could trigger a jump back to dollar/mark's recent peak of 1.7210.
Thom Worden, vice president in the technical analysis group at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, is also looking at the pattern.
"We're forming a head-and-shoulders and it's possible that we go as high as 1.7080 and the formation is still intact," he said.
Worden put supports at 1.6870, 1.6800 and then 1.6710, which he said represents the neckline of the formation.
In dollar/yen, technicians said short-term charts were turning bearish. They said a near-term move above 124 was key for a test of its recent four-year high of 124.82.
"If we get above 124 we could get new highs," said Worden, characterizing that level as a key trendline from the daily highs.
He remains bullish on dollar/yen longer-term, but said a drop below 119.50 would change his perspective.
Worden put near-term support at 122.20. Bank of America's Johnson put near-term resistance in dollar/yen at 123.70, then 124.10.
